chunks: Al-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulman who said: Al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to me from Zayd ibn ʿAlī who said:

Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, revealed to His Prophet, Dāwūd (peace be upon him): 'When My servant remembers Me in his anger, I remember him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all My creation, and I do not cause him to perish along with that which I annihilate.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for remembering God when angry?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, narrated through the chain of Zayd ibn Ali, highlights the spiritual efficacy of dhikr as a mechanism for emotional regulation and divine preservation. It underscores the Shia emphasis on transforming the natural impulse of anger into an act of worship, ensuring that the believer is remembered by God amidst the vast assembly of creation on the Day of Resurrection. The promise of not being 'destroyed' (amhaq) links this specific act of self-restraint to ultimate salvation and stability in the hereafter.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 11.Al-Naḍr narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān who said, “Al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to me from Zayd ibn ʿAlī who said, ‘

Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, revealed to His Prophet, Dāwūd (a), “When My servant remembers Me in his anger [and thereby restrains it], I remember him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all My creation, and I do not cause him to perish along with that which I annihilate.”’”
